title: Sable and the Well
premise: Edmund Underhill, a pest controller who prides himself on never believing in anything, is called to a farmhouse where the infestation leaves fingerprints instead of droppings. The house belongs to dying matriarch Agnes Sable, whose family sold a well decades ago to a man who never signed his half of the papers — and now something in the water is collecting signatures, photographs, and people. As Edmund falls for Agnes's granddaughter Wren, he must choose between the duty of walking away and the justice of finishing what the law refused to: learning the song's last verse without singing along, so the last resident can sign the papers and close the well forever. In the end Edmund sings nothing, signs everything, and drowns the deed — but the chair remains in every photograph, empty, waiting.
about_author: Orsen Dunmore is the pen name of a former rural surveyor who spent fifteen years cataloguing properties no bank would insure. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the things that outlast both.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A routine pest-control job at the Sable farmhouse turns strange: the 'infestation' is greasy handprints climbing the inside of the well shaft. Edmund, professionally skeptical, invoices for rodents. Emotional beat: smug certainty established, first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The prints match no animal; worse, they match each other — same hand, hundreds of times, descending. He returns off-contract, telling himself it's thoroughness. Emotional beat: curiosity masquerading as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Agnes's granddaughter Wren sorts her grandmother's photos for the estate and finds an added wooden chair in every image, growing closer to the camera across decades. Emotional beat: dread arriving through domestic clutter.

chapters.title: Agnes's Terms
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Dying Agnes explains the family curse obliquely: the well was sold in 1948, but the buyer never signed, so the property was never fully transferred — and neither were its debts. She asks Wren to finish the papers. Emotional beat: love tangled with obligation.

chapters.title: Second Visit
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Hired again by Wren, Edmund finds the prints now on the kitchen ceiling, arranged like a seating chart around one empty space. Emotional beat: skepticism curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Song
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren discovers a hymnal with a lullaby missing its final verse, torn out. Agnes hums it in her sleep, always stopping one line short. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by warning.

chapters.title: County Records
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In the archive, Edmund finds the 1948 deed with a signature line left blank and a photograph paper-clipped inside: the extra chair, dated before Wren was born. Emotional beat: the rational world offering no exit.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Records identify the buyer as Elias Mott, who drowned in the well weeks after purchase — unsolved, unburied properly. Emotional beat: history revealing itself as an open wound.

chapters.title: First Night
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren stays over to care for Agnes; at 3 a.m. the chair scrapes across the kitchen floor to sit beside the sleeping woman. Wren doesn't scream; she sits in it. Emotional beat: forbidden intimacy with the haunting.

chapters.title: Underhill's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund's partner notices him photographing ceilings and humming a tune he can't name. He burns the invoice. Emotional beat: corruption beginning — the haunting offering him belonging.

chapters.title: The Verse
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A neighbor recalls the last verse exists only in memory: whoever completes the song invites the singer down. Agnes wakes lucid and begs Wren never to learn it alone. Emotional beat: protection becoming a cage.

chapters.title: Papers
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund locates the unsigned deed's counterpart in Mott's estate box; the signature line has fresh ink that won't dry. Emotional beat: hope with a trapdoor under it.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The presence offers Wren a trade: Agnes's painless passing in exchange for Wren singing the verse at the well. Wren almost says yes. Emotional beat: love against duty, tested.

chapters.title: The Well Opens
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Arriving at dawn, Edmund finds the well cap removed and the water level risen into the yard, reflecting a kitchen that isn't there. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into terror.

chapters.title: Agnes Signs
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Agnes, lucid one last hour, signs her half of the transfer papers and dies smiling — but the document requires two names, and the second line still waits. Emotional beat: grief braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Chair Moves
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The chair appears in Edmund's own apartment photographs now. He understands he's been claimed as a resident-in-waiting. Emotional beat: the skeptic's worldview collapsing inward.

chapters.title: Learning It
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren reconstructs the verse from three half-memories, writing it down without speaking it — the only safe way to carry it. Emotional beat: quiet courage, knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: The Gathering
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. On the anniversary night, the fingerprints converge on the farmhouse; every door opens onto the well shaft. The chair waits at the table set for two. Emotional beat: siege atmosphere, dread peaking.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren realizes 'the last resident' isn't Agnes or herself — it's whoever holds the unfinished deed. She must sign as owner before she can end ownership. Emotional beat: the trap's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: Without Singing Along
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the well, Edmund mouths the verse silently while Wren reads it aloud once, perfectly, as invocation not invitation. The water rises to take them. Emotional beat: climax — discipline against ecstasy.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Submerged in the reflected kitchen, Wren signs the second line with the pen from her grandmother's apron pocket; Elias Mott's hand finally countersigns through hers. The well exhales. Emotional beat: catharsis through completion.

chapters.title: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Weeks later, the farmhouse sells cleanly, the photographs show no chair — except one, kept by Wren, where it sits by a window facing the light. Some doors stay open on purpose. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution, love surviving the haunting.
